notes:
- Mid-market product org (PM + infra) evaluating Hosted first, then Dedicated for predictable unit economics.
- Primary workload: embeddings for "recommendation" index + chat assistant for power users (support + in-product help).
- Latency targets: interactive chat p95 < 500ms (server-side), embedding throughput ~200 qps during cron windows; cost sensitivity high — wants to reduce token costs by >=2x compared to hosted baseline.
- On 2026-03-02 workshop we walked through practical levers: continuous batching, prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts, and quantization profile tradeoffs (fp16 -> 8/4-bit). Customer: "If we can get 2.5x cost improvement without <10% quality drop, we can justify Dedicated commit."
- SE notes (Priya): initial quantized run shows 2.1x inference cost reduction at ~5% drop on abstractive summarization eval set; team wants a deeper eval on in-domain prompts.
- Security: must integrate SSO (SAML) and sign DPA + require audit_logging + KMS for envelope keys. Data residency: primary in US-East; CISO flagged long-term retention policy.
- Procurement: asked for committed capacity pricing tiers and burst policy SLA. Also requested a written fallback policy if Dedicated capacity degraded.
- POC scope agreed: 3-week Dedicated trial with 2 model variants, cost dashboard + unit economics report, and one on-site (virtual) cost-optimization session.
- Quote action: AE to deliver Dedicated pricing draft by 2026-03-15; follow-up workshop to finalize quant settings and rollout plan.
- Quick wins: enable prefix caching for FAQ flows, increase batching window for embedding bulk jobs, try 4-bit quant for smaller models.
- Quote from CTO (call): "We need predictable per-user cost before committing — performance is important but cost is the gating factor."
